relations.definition: A person who is engaged to be married to the object.
relations.embedding_query_text: fiancé of: A person who is engaged to be married to the object. Also called engaged to, betrothed to, future spouse of.

chosen_property.label: fianceOf
chosen_property.definition: Relates a person to their fiancé, the person to whom they are engaged to be married.
chosen_property.justification: No candidate property represents engagement or fiancé relationship between two persons.

candidates.label: spouse
candidates.comment: Relates a person to their legally married partner. Also called "married to", "husband of", "wife of". Examples: [Barack Obama - spouse - Michelle Obama], [Prince Albert - spouse - Queen Victoria], [Marie Curie - spouse - Pierre Curie].

candidates.label: makesOffer
candidates.comment: This property links a subject organization or person to an offer for products or services that they provide. Also called "offers", "provides offer", "sells". Examples: "Retailer X makesOffer 'Discounted Laptop Offer'", "Consultant Y makesOffer 'Hourly Service Offer'", "Restaurant Z makesOffer 'Dinner Menu Offer'".

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: This property indicates the organization, program membership, or member program tier to which a subject person or organization belongs. Also called "belongs to", "is a member of", "affiliated with". Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Sports Club'", "Company X memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Gold Tier Membership'". Distinct from member, which identifies members of an organization or program.

candidates.label: children
candidates.comment: A Person has a Person who is their child. Also called "offspring", "son or daughter", "descendant". Examples: "John Doe" has children "Jane Doe". "Mary Smith" has children "Peter Smith". "Alice Brown" has children "Bob Brown".

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A Product or Service is related to another Product or Service, indicating a general connection or association. Also called "associated with", "connected to", "linked to". Examples: "Product A isRelatedTo Product B (e.g., complementary products).", "Service X isRelatedTo Service Y (e.g., bundled services).", "The software isRelatedTo a specific hardware device." Distinct from `isSimilarTo`, which implies functional similarity.

relations.definition: The geographical or administrative place where the subject entity is situated.
relations.embedding_query_text: located in: The geographical or administrative place where the subject entity is situated. Also called situated in, based in, positioned in.

chosen_property.label: containedIn
chosen_property.justification: containedIn models a Place (such as an EventVenue) being contained within another Place (such as a City).

instances: Madison Square Garden -> New York City

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A Place is contained within another Place. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "Paris" is containedIn "France". "California" is containedIn "United States". "The Louvre" is containedIn "Paris".

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A Place is contained within another Place. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "Paris" is containedInPlace "France". "California" is containedInPlace "United States". "The Louvre" is containedInPlace "Paris".

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: This property indicates the physical or virtual place where a subject action, event, interaction counter, or organization is situated or occurs. Also called "venue", "address", "site". Examples: "Concert Event location 'Madison Square Garden'", "Company Headquarters location '123 Main St, Anytown'", "Online Meeting location 'Zoom Link'". Distinct from locationCreated, which specifies where a creative work was originally made.

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: An Organization has a foundingLocation, which is the specific place where it was established. Also called "place of origin", "establishment location", "birthplace". Examples: "The Organization's foundingLocation is 'Menlo Park, California'.", "This company's foundingLocation is 'a garage in Silicon Valley'.", "The foundingLocation of the university is 'Cambridge, England'." Distinct from location, which is a general current location.

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: Relates a medical study to the administrative area or geographic location where it is conducted. Also called "trial location", "study site location", "geographic study area". Examples: [Vaccine Trial - studyLocation - California], [Diabetes Study - studyLocation - United Kingdom], [Oncology Study - studyLocation - Tokyo].

relations.definition: A sports player who is a member of or competes on behalf of the object team or country.
relations.embedding_query_text: plays for: A sports player who is a member of or competes on behalf of the object team or country. Also called represents, competes for, member of.

chosen_property.label: playsFor
chosen_property.definition: Relates a sports player to the team or country for which they play or compete.
chosen_property.justification: The candidate 'athlete' has the reverse subject-object direction, and other candidates do not fit.

candidates.label: athlete
candidates.comment: A SportsTeam has an athlete who is a Person playing as a member of the team. Also called team member, player, sports person. Examples: The Lakers have athlete 'LeBron James', The national soccer team has athlete 'Lionel Messi', The Warriors have athlete 'Stephen Curry'.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A SportsEvent features a Person or SportsTeam who is a competitor in the event. Also called "participant", "opponent", "player". Examples: A sports event has competitor "Team A". A sports event has competitor "John Doe". A sports event has competitor "Los Angeles Lakers".

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: Relates an exercise action to the sports team that participated in the action. Also called "participating team", "represented team", "sports team participant". Examples: [Passing Action - sportsTeam - Real Madrid], [Touchdown Action - sportsTeam - New England Patriots], [Rowing Action - sportsTeam - Oxford Rowing Club].

candidates.label: sport
candidates.comment: Relates a sports event or sports organization to the specific sport or athletic game it is associated with. Also called "associated sport", "type of sport", "played sport". Examples: [World Series - sport - "Baseball"], [FIFA - sport - "Soccer"], [Wimbledon - sport - "Tennis"].

candidates.label: awayTeam
candidates.comment: A SportsEvent has an awayTeam which is the Person or SportsTeam designated as the visiting competitor. Also called visiting team, opponent team, guest team. Examples: A soccer match has awayTeam 'Manchester United', The basketball game features awayTeam 'Golden State Warriors', The tennis match has awayTeam 'Serena Williams'. Distinct from homeTeam, which is the host competitor.

relations.definition: The official role, job title, or political office held by the subject.
relations.embedding_query_text: held position: The official role, job title, or political office held by the subject. Also called served as, holds office of, occupied role of.

chosen_property.label: jobTitle
chosen_property.justification: jobTitle links a Person to their professional role or position held.

instances: Zohran Mamdani -> New York City Mayor

candidates.label: jobTitle
candidates.comment: A Person has a job title, which is a DefinedTerm or Text, describing their professional role. Also called "professional title", "position held", "occupation". Examples: "The Person has a jobTitle 'Financial Manager'.", "Her jobTitle is 'Senior Software Engineer'.", "The Person's jobTitle is 'Chief Executive Officer'."

candidates.label: namedPosition
candidates.comment: A Role specifies a named position, which is the particular position played or filled by a person or organization within a larger organization. Also called role title, position held, job title. Examples: A player's role has named position 'Quarterback'. An employee's role has named position 'Senior Software Engineer'. A board member's role has named position 'Treasurer'. Distinct from roleName, which is a more general description of the role.

candidates.label: responsibilities
candidates.comment: Relates a job posting or occupation to the textual description of duties and responsibilities associated with the role. Also called "job duties", "role responsibilities", "tasks required". Examples: [Software Engineer Posting - responsibilities - "Write clean code and maintain APIs"], [Nurse Occupation - responsibilities - "Provide patient care and administer medication"], [Manager Posting - responsibilities - "Lead team meetings and set quarterly goals"].

candidates.label: title
candidates.comment: Relates a job posting to the official name or designation of the employment position. Also called 'job title', 'position name', 'role designation'. Examples: [SoftwareEngineerPosting - title - 'Senior Full-Stack Developer'], [NurseVacancy - title - 'Registered Nurse (ICU)'], [SalesRole - title - 'Account Executive'].

candidates.label: roleName
candidates.comment: Relates a role to the textual name or title of the position played or performed. Also called "role title", "position name", "job title in role". Examples: [Inker Role - roleName - "Inker"], [Quarterback Role - roleName - "Quarterback"], [Lead Actor Role - roleName - "Protagonist"].

relations.definition: The subject brought the object media or work into existence.
relations.embedding_query_text: created: The subject brought the object media or work into existence. Also called authored, developed, produced.

chosen_property.label: created
chosen_property.definition: Relates a person to a creative work or media that they brought into existence.
chosen_property.justification: None of the candidates express the relationship of a person creating a creative work.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: Relates any thing to a creative work or event that is about or describes it. Also called "described in", "subject of work", "featured in". Examples: [Albert Einstein - subjectOf - Biography Book], [Solar Eclipse - subjectOf - Science Documentary], [New Product - subjectOf - Launch Event].

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: produces is the Thing that is the tangible outcome or output generated by a Service. Also called generates, yields, results in, creates. Examples: A passport application service produces a passport. A permit application service produces a building permit. A printing service produces printed documents.

candidates.label: material
candidates.comment: This property specifies the material, as a product, text, or URL, from which a subject creative work or product is made. Also called "made of", "composed of", "fabric". Examples: "Jacket material 'Leather'", "Book material 'Paper'", "Sculpture material 'Bronze'".

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: Relates a creative work, event, or term to the subject matter or topic it describes. Also called "subject matter of", "topic of", "focuses on", "covers". Examples: [Book "The Hobbit" - about - "Middle-earth"], [Lecture - about - "Quantum Physics"], [Article - about - "Climate Change"]. Distinct from mainEntity, which is the primary, singular topic that the page or work is explicitly a representation of.

candidates.label: workFeatured
candidates.comment: Relates an event to a creative work that is showcased, exhibited, or highlighted during the event. Also called "featured work", "showcased creation", "exhibited piece". Examples: "Art Exhibition 2023 - workFeatured - Starry Night", "Film Festival - workFeatured - Pulp Fiction", "Book Launch - workFeatured - The Promise". Distinct from workPerformed, which is specifically a work that is actively performed (like a play or concert) during the event.

relations.definition: A person sharing one or both parents with the object.
relations.embedding_query_text: sibling of: A person sharing one or both parents with the object. Also called brother of, sister of, related to as sibling.

chosen_property.label: sibling
chosen_property.justification: sibling directly connects a person to another person who is their sibling.

candidates.label: sibling
candidates.comment: Relates a person to one of their siblings. Also called "brother or sister", "sibling of", "has sibling". Examples: [Prince William - sibling - Prince Harry], [Venus Williams - sibling - Serena Williams], [Luke Skywalker - sibling - Leia Organa]. Distinct from siblings, which is a plural variant.

candidates.label: siblings
candidates.comment: Relates a person to their siblings. Also called "brothers and sisters", "has siblings", "sibling list". Examples: [Prince William - siblings - Prince Harry], [Venus Williams - siblings - Serena Williams], [Luke Skywalker - siblings - Leia Organa]. Distinct from sibling, which is the singular variant.

candidates.label: children
candidates.comment: A Person has a Person who is their child. Also called "offspring", "son or daughter", "descendant". Examples: "John Doe" has children "Jane Doe". "Mary Smith" has children "Peter Smith". "Alice Brown" has children "Bob Brown".

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A Person has a generic familial relation to another Person. Also called 'family relation', 'kin'. Examples: 'John is related to 'Jane'.' 'She is related to 'her cousin'.' 'The person is related to 'their sibling'.' 'He is related to 'his aunt'.'

candidates.label: parent
candidates.comment: A Person has a parent, who is an individual from whom they are descended. Also called is child of, mother, father. Examples: Alice has parent 'Bob'. John has parent 'Mary'. A child has parent 'their biological mother'. Distinct from children, which is the inverse property.

relations.definition: A person who produces artistic or musical work for the object.
relations.embedding_query_text: producer of: A person who produces artistic or musical work for the object. Also called music producer for, collaborator with.

chosen_property.label: producerOf
chosen_property.definition: Relates a music or artistic producer to the artist or person whose work they produce.
chosen_property.justification: The candidate 'producer' relates a CreativeWork to its producer, whereas this relation connects a producer person to an artist person.

candidates.label: producer
candidates.comment: A producer is the Organization or Person responsible for overseeing the creation and production of a CreativeWork, such as a movie or music album. Also called made by, created by, executive producer, production company. Examples: A movie producer Steven Spielberg. A music album producer Columbia Records. A TV series producer Shonda Rhimes. Distinct from director, who guides the artistic and dramatic aspects, and creator, who originates the work.

candidates.label: album
candidates.comment: Relates a music group or artist to a music album they produced. Also called "music album", "produced album", "released album". Examples: [MusicGroup "The Beatles" - album - MusicAlbum "Abbey Road"], [Artist "Taylor Swift" - album - MusicAlbum "Midnights"], [Band "Pink Floyd" - album - MusicAlbum "The Dark Side of the Moon"]. Distinct from albums, which is a plural collection relation.

candidates.label: composer
candidates.comment: A MusicComposition or an Event featuring music has an Organization or Person who wrote the musical piece. Also called "written by", "composed by", "music by". Examples: The composition "Symphony No. 5" has composer "Ludwig van Beethoven". The musical "Hamilton" has composer "Lin-Manuel Miranda". The song "Bohemian Rhapsody" has composer "Freddie Mercury". Distinct from `byArtist`, which is the person or group who performed the work.

candidates.label: sdPublisher
candidates.comment: Relates a creative work to the organization or person responsible for generating and publishing its structured data markup. Also called "metadata publisher", "structured data creator", "markup publisher". Examples: [Aggregated Event Page - sdPublisher - Event Aggregator Corp], [Student Project Page - sdPublisher - Jane Doe], [Open Data Portal - sdPublisher - City Government].

candidates.label: albumProductionType
candidates.comment: Relates a music album to its production classification, such as a studio, live, or soundtrack album. Also called "production type", "album format", "recording type". Examples: [Album "Abbey Road" - albumProductionType - "StudioAlbum"], [Album "MTV Unplugged" - albumProductionType - "LiveAlbum"], [Album "Star Wars OST" - albumProductionType - "Soundtrack"].

relations.definition: A person responsible for managing public relations and press for the object.
relations.embedding_query_text: publicist of: A person responsible for managing public relations and press for the object. Also called press officer for, media representative for.

chosen_property.label: publicistOf
chosen_property.definition: Relates a publicist to the person or entity whose public relations they manage.
chosen_property.justification: No candidate property represents a publicist managing public relations for a person.

candidates.label: accountablePerson
candidates.comment: Relates a creative work to the person who is legally responsible or accountable for its content. Also called "legally responsible person", "accountable party", "responsible editor". Examples: [News Article - accountablePerson - Person "Jane Doe"], [Corporate Report - accountablePerson - Person "John Smith"], [Medical Guide - accountablePerson - Person "Dr. Alice Green"].

candidates.label: sdPublisher
candidates.comment: Relates a creative work to the organization or person responsible for generating and publishing its structured data markup. Also called "metadata publisher", "structured data creator", "markup publisher". Examples: [Aggregated Event Page - sdPublisher - Event Aggregator Corp], [Student Project Page - sdPublisher - Jane Doe], [Open Data Portal - sdPublisher - City Government].

candidates.label: broadcaster
candidates.comment: A BroadcastService is operated or owned by an Organization that acts as its broadcaster. Also called "operated by", "owned by", "broadcast by", "station owner". Examples: "BBC One" has broadcaster "British Broadcasting Corporation". "CNN" has broadcaster "Warner Bros. Discovery". "NPR" has broadcaster "National Public Radio".

candidates.label: maintainer
candidates.comment: This property identifies the person or organization responsible for managing contributions to and/or publication of a subject creative work, such as a dataset or software package. Also called "managed by", "curated by", "supported by". Examples: "Software Package A maintainer 'Open Source Community'", "Dataset B maintainer 'University Research Group'", "Project C maintainer 'John Doe'".

candidates.label: producer
candidates.comment: A producer is the Organization or Person responsible for overseeing the creation and production of a CreativeWork, such as a movie or music album. Also called made by, created by, executive producer, production company. Examples: A movie producer Steven Spielberg. A music album producer Columbia Records. A TV series producer Shonda Rhimes. Distinct from director, who guides the artistic and dramatic aspects, and creator, who originates the work.

relations.definition: An individual enrolled in and studying at an educational institution.
relations.embedding_query_text: student at: An individual enrolled in and studying at an educational institution. Also called attending, enrolled at, studies at.

chosen_property.label: alumniOf
chosen_property.justification: alumniOf connects a Person to an educational organization they attend or attended.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: Relates a person to an educational organization or other organization they graduated from or attended. Also called "graduated from", "attended school at", "former student of". Examples: [Person "Barack Obama" - alumniOf - "Columbia University"], [Person "Elon Musk" - alumniOf - "University of Pennsylvania"], [Person "Emma Watson" - alumniOf - "Brown University"]. Distinct from alumni, which is the inverse relation mapping an organization to its graduates.

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: Relates an educational organization or other organization to a person who graduated from or attended it. Also called "graduates", "former students", "alumni members". Examples: [Harvard University - alumni - Person "Bill Gates"], [Stanford University - alumni - Person "Larry Page"], [High School - alumni - Person "Jane Doe"]. Distinct from alumniOf, which is the inverse relation mapping a Person to their school.

candidates.label: financialAidEligible
candidates.comment: A Course or EducationalOccupationalProgram is financialAidEligible for a specific type or program of financial assistance that students can use for tuition or fees. Also called "eligible for financial aid", "financial assistance program", "aid program". Examples: "The Course is financialAidEligible for 'Pell Grants'.", "This EducationalOccupationalProgram is financialAidEligible for 'federal student loans'.", "The program is financialAidEligible for 'scholarships'."

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: This property identifies an organization or person who is a member of a subject organization or program membership. Also called "has member", "includes member", "comprises member". Examples: "Club A member 'John Doe'", "Company B member 'Subsidiary C'", "ProgramMembership X member 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from memberOf, which indicates the organization or program a person/organization belongs to.

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: Relates a person to an organization, such as a school, club, or employer, with which they are formally associated. Also called "affiliated with", "member of", "associated organization". Examples: [Professor - affiliation - "Stanford University"], [Athlete - affiliation - "Los Angeles Lakers"], [Researcher - affiliation - "CERN"].

relations.definition: An employee or journalist employed by or affiliated with the object organization.
relations.embedding_query_text: works for: An employee or journalist employed by or affiliated with the object organization. Also called employed by, staff member at, affiliated with.

chosen_property.label: worksFor
chosen_property.justification: worksFor directly connects a Person to the Organization that employs them.

candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An Organization has an employee, who is a person working for that organization. Also called "staff member", "worker". Examples: "The company has employee 'Jane Doe'", "The organization lists 'John Smith' as an employee", "'Alice Brown' is an employee of the firm.".

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: Relates a person to an organization that employs them or for which they perform services. Also called "employed by", "employee of", "works at", "affiliated with". Examples: "Sundar Pichai - worksFor - Google", "Jane Doe - worksFor - Red Cross", "Professor Green - worksFor - Oxford University".

candidates.label: employees
candidates.comment: An Organization has employees, who are people working for that organization. Also called "staff", "workforce". Examples: "The company has employees 'Jane Doe' and 'John Smith'", "The organization lists its employees", "The firm's employees are dedicated.". Distinct from employee, which typically refers to a single person.

candidates.label: colleague
candidates.comment: A Person has a Person or URL representing a colleague. Also called "co-worker", "associate", "professional peer". Examples: "John Doe" has colleague "Jane Smith". "Mary Lee" has colleague "https://example.com/bob". "Peter Jones" has colleague "Sarah Brown".

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: Relates a person to an organization, such as a school, club, or employer, with which they are formally associated. Also called "affiliated with", "member of", "associated organization". Examples: [Professor - affiliation - "Stanford University"], [Athlete - affiliation - "Los Angeles Lakers"], [Researcher - affiliation - "CERN"].

relations.definition: The country of origin or nationality of the subject person.
relations.embedding_query_text: from country: The country of origin or nationality of the subject person. Also called native of, originating from, hails from.

chosen_property.label: nationality
chosen_property.justification: nationality links a Person to the Country of their citizenship or origin.

candidates.label: nationality
candidates.comment: A Person holds a specific nationality, indicating the country of their citizenship or origin. Also called is a national of, citizenship, country of origin. Examples: John Doe has nationality 'United States'. Marie Curie had nationality 'Poland'. A traveler has nationality 'Germany'. Distinct from birthPlace, which is where the person was born.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork or Product has a countryOfOrigin, which specifies the country from which it originates. Also called origin country, nation of origin, produced in. Examples: "French Wine" countryOfOrigin "France", "Japanese Anime" countryOfOrigin "Japan", "German Car" countryOfOrigin "Germany". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where a product was assembled, and countryOfLastProcessing, which indicates where it was last processed before import.

candidates.label: birthPlace
candidates.comment: A Person has a birthPlace which is the Place where they were born. Also called place of birth, born in, birth location. Examples: A person has birthPlace 'London', John Doe's birthPlace is 'New York City', Her birthPlace is 'Paris, France'.

candidates.label: parent
candidates.comment: A Person has a parent, who is an individual from whom they are descended. Also called is child of, mother, father. Examples: Alice has parent 'Bob'. John has parent 'Mary'. A child has parent 'their biological mother'. Distinct from children, which is the inverse property.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: Relates a person to an educational organization or other organization they graduated from or attended. Also called "graduated from", "attended school at", "former student of". Examples: [Person "Barack Obama" - alumniOf - "Columbia University"], [Person "Elon Musk" - alumniOf - "University of Pennsylvania"], [Person "Emma Watson" - alumniOf - "Brown University"]. Distinct from alumni, which is the inverse relation mapping an organization to its graduates.
